correctness.rationale: The unweighted 20-vertex Legendre Gram is reduced by antipodal parity to a ten-dimensional signed/unsigned association scheme. Every integer matrix identity is independently reconstructed from exact Q(sqrt(5)) coordinates in the included standard-library verifier. The quadratic adjacency relations yield the six eigenvalue expressions and multiplicities. The analytic Laplace-integral bound on Legendre polynomials gives strict positivity in every compatible branch for all l>=186; exact rational recurrence and comparisons (186 degrees, l=0..185) prove the complete exception list. The addition theorem fixes the evaluation normalization. Neither numerical sampling nor finite enumeration is substituted for the analytic infinite tail.

value.rationale: The 20-vertex regular dodecahedron is a natural, maximally symmetric five-design for spherical sampling. Exact eigenvalues give every fixed-degree least-squares singular spectrum; unexpectedly, rank drops from 9 at degree 4 to 6 at degree 5 and remains defective at degrees 8 and 14, despite naive dimension growth. The rigorously sharp all-degree cutoff at 15 establishes eventual interpolation of arbitrary antipodal-compatible data by each single-degree harmonic, useful for interpolation and covariance identifiability. This is an exact natural classification, not a routine coordinate renaming or a finite table recomputation alone.
